item.content:encoded: The National Hurricane Center has issued a Hurricane and Storm Surge Watch for the Gulf Coast, according to WPMI NBC 15. The watch indicates that hurricane conditions and significant storm surge are possible in the watch area within the next 48 hours. Residents in coastal Escambia County, Santa Rosa County, and the broader Gulf Coast region should monitor the National Hurricane Center's updates closely and begin preparations if they are in the affected area. Additional details about the specific timing, expected intensity, and affected counties should be confirmed through the latest National Hurricane Center advisory.

item.title: Hurricane Watch issued for Pensacola-area coastal waters
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The watch applies to waters extending 20 nautical miles offshore from the Okaloosa-Walton line through Pensacola, as well as waters 20 to 60…
item.content:encoded:
The National Weather Service has issued a Hurricane Watch for coastal waters stretching from the Okaloosa-Walton County line to Pascagoula, Mississippi, according to alert information posted by the service. The watch applies to waters extending 20 nautical miles offshore from the Okaloosa-Walton line through Pensacola, as well as waters 20 to 60 nautical miles out from the Okaloosa-Walton area to Pensacola.

A Hurricane Watch means hurricane conditions are possible within the watch area, typically within 48 hours of issuance. Mariners and coastal residents in Escambia, Santa Rosa, and Okaloosa counties should monitor the latest forecast updates and prepare accordingly.

The National Weather Service continues to track the system and will issue updated watches, warnings, and forecasts as conditions develop.

item.title: PSC hosts fifth annual walk honoring slain professor Carla Williams
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola State College will hold its fifth annual Domestic Violence Awareness & Remembrance Walk on October 22 at 4 p.m. on the track at its Pensacola campus, honoring the memory of associate professor Carla E. Williams, who was killed by domestic violence in May 2021. Williams had spent more than 24 years at PSC working in athletics, Collegiate…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola State College will hold its fifth annual Domestic Violence Awareness & Remembrance Walk on October 22 at 4 p.m. on the track at its Pensacola campus, honoring the memory of associate professor Carla E. Williams, who was killed by domestic violence in May 2021.

Williams had spent more than 24 years at PSC working in athletics, Collegiate High, and the Mathematics and Computer Science Department. She was also a former PSC Lady Pirate basketball player. The annual walk has become a key part of how the college community memorializes her and raises awareness about domestic violence.

"Domestic violence is an ongoing issue in our society and in 2021, it really hit home for the PSC family with the loss of Coach Carla Williams," said Lynsey Listau, dean of students at Pensacola State College, according to a college press release. "To honor Carla and other victims of domestic violence, we've scheduled the fifth annual walk to raise awareness of the issue and provide information on the resources available to help victims."

The walk takes place during October, designated as Domestic Violence Awareness Month nationwide. PSC students can participate free; nonstudents pay a $10 fee. T-shirts will be available for $20 while supplies last. All proceeds benefit the Carla Williams Memorial Scholarship Fund. Registration is available at athletics.pensacolastate.edu/Carla_Williams_Walk.

item.title: Senator Moody Hosts 60+ Florida Veterans on Honor Flight to D.C.
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Senator Ashley Moody welcomed more than 60 Florida veterans to Washington, D.C. this week as part of an Honor Flight trip, meeting with the group at the Lincoln Memorial to thank them for their service. "Florida is home to some of the bravest men and women who answered the call to serve our nation," Moody said in remarks at the memorial. "We will…
item.content:encoded:
Senator Ashley Moody welcomed more than 60 Florida veterans to Washington, D.C. this week as part of an Honor Flight trip, meeting with the group at the Lincoln Memorial to thank them for their service. "Florida is home to some of the bravest men and women who answered the call to serve our nation," Moody said in remarks at the memorial. "We will ensure their service will never be forgotten."

Honor Flights are organized trips that bring veterans from across the country to the nation's capital to visit war memorials and monuments dedicated to their service. Florida is home to more than 1.4 million veterans, one of the largest veteran populations in the nation. Earlier this year, the Florida Veterans Foundation awarded Villages Honor Flight a $15,000 grant as part of its broader support for 10 Honor Flight hubs operating across the state.

Since joining the U.S. Senate, Moody has established herself as a vocal advocate for military members and veterans. She recently joined the Senate Armed Services Committee and has cosponsored legislation including the Veterans Bill of Rights Act, which would ensure veterans are clearly informed of their existing rights regarding VA health care and benefits. Moody also received a briefing at NAS Pensacola earlier this year, where she discussed the critical importance of the Navy and Coast Guard presence in the Florida Panhandle ahead of the 200th anniversary of naval operations in the region.

item.content:encoded:
The 53rd annual National Shrimp Festival in Gulf Shores, Alabama, has been canceled due to the expected arrival of Hurricane Isaias this weekend, according to WKRG News 5. The festival, which had been scheduled to run Thursday through Sunday, was called off as the Gulf Coast prepares for the storm's impact.

The cancellation affects one of the region's major fall events, which typically draws thousands of visitors to the Alabama coast. Festival organizers decided to prioritize public safety as Hurricane Isaias approaches the area.

item.content:encoded:
A 19-year-old Loxley, Alabama man has been sentenced to time served for making a threat over the internet, according to a Department of Justice news release. Robert Davian Grijalva has been in custody since 2025 and will be released, having completed his sentence through jail time already served.

The case was prosecuted under federal law governing threatening communications made online. Grijalva's sentencing resolves the matter.

Northeastern winds are blowing at 21.4 knots, driving the elevated seas across the Gulf. Air temperatures at the buoy are holding around 79.5 degrees Fahrenheit. The conditions…
item.content:encoded:
Buoy 42039, anchored off the Pensacola coast, is recording significant wave heights of 6.2 feet Wednesday, according to real-time marine data shared by Florida Gulf Signal. Northeastern winds are blowing at 21.4 knots, driving the elevated seas across the Gulf.

Air temperatures at the buoy are holding around 79.5 degrees Fahrenheit. The conditions reflect typical autumn Gulf activity as wind patterns shift with the season.

Boaters and beachgoers should exercise caution in the elevated surf, particularly on the western side of Escambia and Santa Rosa County beaches where northeast winds tend to pile water onto the shore.

item.title: Taddeo Wins genCLEO Action Endorsement in CFO Race
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Former State Senator Annette Taddeo, the Democratic nominee for Florida Chief Financial Officer, has secured an endorsement from genCLEO Action, a youth-led organization focused on climate action and clean energy. The group cited Taddeo's commitment to environmental protection and her stance against major polluters as reasons for the backing.…
item.content:encoded:
Former State Senator Annette Taddeo, the Democratic nominee for Florida Chief Financial Officer, has secured an endorsement from genCLEO Action, a youth-led organization focused on climate action and clean energy. The group cited Taddeo's commitment to environmental protection and her stance against major polluters as reasons for the backing.

"Young Floridians understand that the decisions made in Florida today will shape whether we can afford to build a future here," said Raymer Maguire, VP of Campaigns for genCLEO Action. Taddeo emphasized that as CFO, she would prioritize accountability and responsible financial decisions that protect Florida's natural resources, particularly as the state continues to attract energy-intensive industries like data centers and artificial intelligence operations.

Taddeo's endorsement roster has grown to include prominent Florida Democrats, including Miami-Dade County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava, Orange County Mayor Jerry Demings, former CFO Alex Sink, and U.S. Congresswoman Donna Shalala. She has also earned backing from major labor unions, environmental groups, and gun safety advocates. A Colombian immigrant who fled violence as a teenager, Taddeo flipped a Republican-held Florida Senate seat in 2017 and was reelected by six points in 2020.

Tropical Storm Isaias is expected to intensify into a hurricane before making landfall…
item.content:encoded:
Eglin Air Force Base has declared Hurricane Condition 4 as Tropical Storm Isaias forms in the Gulf of Mexico, according to WKRG News 5. The alert means destructive winds of 58 mph or greater are possible within the next 72 hours, the base said in a news release.

Tropical Storm Isaias is expected to intensify into a hurricane before making landfall in the region. The declaration puts Eglin on heightened alert, triggering storm preparation protocols across the base in Okaloosa County.

The condition level is part of the Air Force's hurricane readiness scale, which allows military installations to stage resources, secure facilities, and coordinate with local emergency management ahead of tropical weather threats.

This marks the latest weather concern for the region as the Atlantic hurricane season continues through November.

Fans and families planning to attend games should note the new Thursday night kickoff times. For specific game times and locations, contact your local school's athletic department.

item.title: DeSantis declares state of emergency for 25 Florida counties ahead of Tropical Depression Nine
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis signed an executive order Tuesday declaring a state of emergency for 25 Florida counties, including Escambia and Santa Rosa, as Tropical Depression Nine approaches the Gulf Coast. The order allows the Florida Division of Emergency Management to stage critical resources and prepare for potential impacts expected later this…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis signed an executive order Tuesday declaring a state of emergency for 25 Florida counties, including Escambia and Santa Rosa, as Tropical Depression Nine approaches the Gulf Coast. The order allows the Florida Division of Emergency Management to stage critical resources and prepare for potential impacts expected later this week.

According to the governor's office, the storm is forecast to strengthen into a tropical storm or hurricane with possible landfall along the central Gulf Coast. North Florida, including the Pensacola area, faces threats of heavy rainfall, strong winds, coastal flooding, and isolated tornadoes. State officials warn that recent significant rainfall has already saturated soils across the region, raising the risk of flash flooding.

The Florida State Emergency Response Team is mobilizing resources staged in Tallahassee and the Santa Rosa area, including generators, fuel, flood barriers, boxed water, shelf-stable meals, tarps, sandbags, and other emergency supplies. The state of emergency also covers Baker, Bay, Calhoun, Columbia, Dixie, Franklin, Gadsden, Gilchrist, Gulf, Hamilton, Holmes, Jackson, Jefferson, Lafayette, Leon, Liberty, Madison, Okaloosa, Suwannee, Taylor, Walton, Wakulla, and Washington counties.

DeSantis urged Floridians to finalize disaster plans and stock hurricane supply kits now. More information and preparedness resources are available at FloridaDisaster.org, and residents can follow @FLSERT on X for live storm updates.

item.content:encoded:
Escambia County is offering free sand to residents preparing for potential tropical weather, joining Foley and Okaloosa County in making the material available as hurricane season continues through November.

The move comes as communities along the Gulf Coast take preemptive steps to help residents protect their properties. Sandbags are commonly used to reinforce barriers around homes and businesses during severe weather events.

According to WKRG-TV 5, residents can obtain sand from the county during the distribution period. Details on specific distribution locations and hours are available through Escambia County Emergency Management. Residents should check with the county for current availability and any requirements for pickup.

item.title: Santa Rosa County bracing for heavy rain, flash flooding risk from Tropical Depression Nine
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County Public Safety is monitoring Tropical Depression Nine as it approaches the region, with forecasters warning of heavy rain and potential flash flooding late this week and over the weekend. The extent of impacts will depend on the storm's exact track, but Santa Rosa County is under a slight risk for flash flooding Friday, October 9,…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County Public Safety is monitoring Tropical Depression Nine as it approaches the region, with forecasters warning of heavy rain and potential flash flooding late this week and over the weekend. The extent of impacts will depend on the storm's exact track, but Santa Rosa County is under a slight risk for flash flooding Friday, October 9, and Saturday, October 10, according to a county alert issued Tuesday afternoon.

Heavy rainfall poses the greatest threat, particularly in urban areas or locations where storms repeatedly move over the same spots. The National Weather Service warns that flash flooding could affect low-lying areas, underpasses, and places with poor drainage. A high rip current risk is also in effect for Navarre Beach through at least Saturday, and county officials are reminding beachgoers never to swim without a lifeguard present.

Santa Rosa County Public Works is offering free sand on a first-come, first-served basis at four locations: the corner of Leisure Street and Citrus Drive in Navarre, Tiger Point Park in Gulf Breeze (1370 Tiger Park Lane), Pace Fire-Rescue (4773 Pace Patriot Boulevard), and the corner of Pine Forest Road and Carroll Road in Milton. Residents must provide their own sandbags and shovels, though bags can be purchased at local hardware stores. County officials stress that sandbags offer limited protection and recommend residents obtain flood insurance — which carries a mandatory 30-day waiting period.

Residents in flood-prone areas should know their evacuation zones, maintain disaster supply kits, and keep vehicle gas tanks at least half full. County officials also recommend clearing gutters and downspouts, trimming trees, and ensuring all family members have a weather alert plan in place. Real-time weather updates are available at weather.gov/mob and through AlertSantaRosa.com.

item.title: Senator Moody announces $44M in federal fire grants for Florida departments
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Senator Ashley Moody announced more than $44 million in federal grant funding for fire departments across Florida on Tuesday during National Fire Prevention Week, with the Lehigh Acres Fire Control and Rescue District receiving $4.2 million to hire 21 new firefighters. The funding comes through the federal Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency…
item.content:encoded:
Senator Ashley Moody announced more than $44 million in federal grant funding for fire departments across Florida on Tuesday during National Fire Prevention Week, with the Lehigh Acres Fire Control and Rescue District receiving $4.2 million to hire 21 new firefighters.

The funding comes through the federal Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) grant program, which helps departments hire personnel and acquire equipment. The announcement was made in Lehigh Acres as Florida enters its historically active dry season for wildfires.

According to Moody's office, Florida has faced significant wildfire activity in recent years. So far in 2026, the state has recorded approximately 2,975 wildfires burning more than 280,000 acres. Last year, Florida experienced 2,913 wildfires that burned more than 228,000 acres, including a major wildfire outside Miami earlier in the summer.

Since Moody took office, Florida fire departments have received more than $89 million in total firefighter grant awards across three separate FEMA programs. With Florida serving as the nation's lightning capital and nearly half the state covered in fire-prone forests, state officials continue emphasizing fire prevention measures including regular smoke alarm testing, yard maintenance, and emergency preparedness planning.
